description: Make the model picker actually populate, refresh on provider-config changes, and surface enumeration errors + a diagnostics/refresh affordance so failures are never silent. This is the coherent, shippable fix for the confirmed root cause: (bug A) providers.load() is never triggered on app startup or when the chat picker mounts (only Settings > Providers & Keys calls it), so the chat picker store starts empty and stays empty; and (bug B) the backend never emits CoreEvent::ProvidersChanged, so even saving a key/runtime never refetches. Fix both, then make errors visible near the chat picker and add an always-available Refresh affordance. Depends on FEAT-001 (baseline + confirmed inventory). Scope EXCLUDES the embedded-engine folder-scan rework and any feature-flag/release-bundle changes (out of scope per orchestrator). USER STEERING (2026): user reconfirmed the exact symptom - after filling in model + API key details (they persist), NOTHING reflects in the conversation and the chat picker still shows 'No models available yet. Add a provider under Settings > Providers & Keys or start a local runtime to get started.' That is precisely bug A + bug B and is what this feature fixes. User asked 'Would building ollama right in fix some of this?' - the answer is NO and must NOT be pursued here: Ollama is already integrated (ensure_ollama_provider_config seeds it and enumerates via GET /api/tags); a reachable Ollama shows nothing for the SAME frontend reason (the picker store is never load()-ed), so embedding/bundling Ollama would not fix the picker and is out of scope. User also said to scrap the HTML5-rewrite idea: stay on Tauri (already the constraint; no action needed).
steps: STARTUP LOAD (bug A): In frontend/src/app.tsx, trigger the providers store's load() once at app startup so the chat picker is populated when the app opens. Do it in the existing top-level useEffect ALONGSIDE the onCoreEvent subscription (read useProvidersStore.getState().load and call it, void-ed), mirroring how AgentEditor.tsx/ToolManager.tsx/History.tsx load their stores on mount. CRITICAL: keep the SINGLE onCoreEvent subscription semantics intact - EMPTY deps, opened once, torn down once (do not add deps that re-run it). Do not introduce a second subscription. Keep the fan-out to every store's applyCoreEvent unchanged.

STORE (optional, only if it makes the Refresh affordance cleaner): frontend/src/state/providers.ts already exposes load(). If a components-facing 'refresh' action reads more naturally than calling getState().load(), you MAY add a thin alias, but prefer reusing load() to avoid store-shape churn. Do NOT change the { models, errors } shape or the applyCoreEvent 'providersChanged' refetch.

BACKEND REFRESH EMIT (bug B) - route (a), chosen because AppState.core_events (UnboundedSender<CoreEvent>) is already available to command handlers and already used for McpStateChanged/McpError: In crates/tauri-app/src/commands.rs, after each SUCCESSFUL provider-config mutation, emit CoreEvent::ProvidersChanged via the sender: `let _ = state.core_events.send(orchestrator_core::CoreEvent::ProvidersChanged);` (fire-and-forget, mirroring the existing McpStateChanged sends; a dropped UI event must not fail the command). Wire it for: set_cloud_provider, clear_cloud_provider, set_local_runtime, clear_local_runtime, import_embedded_model, select_embedded_model, and the embedded active-model changes load_embedded_model / unload_embedded_model (these change what enumerates/what is loaded under Local). The #[tauri::command] wrappers hold `state: tauri::State<AppState>` and delegate to _inner(&state,...); emit in the wrapper AFTER the _inner call returns Ok (so a validation/persist error emits nothing), OR pass state into _inner and emit at the end - choose the least-invasive; emitting in the thin wrapper on Ok keeps the _inner unit tests (which drive _inner directly) unchanged. Ensure `orchestrator_core::CoreEvent` is in scope (it is already referenced in commands.rs).

REMOVE DEAD-CODE ALLOW: In crates/orchestrator-core/src/events.rs, now that ProvidersChanged is emitted, remove its `#[allow(dead_code)]` attribute and the 'no emitter wired yet' comment (the module header says to drop each as its emitter lands). Leave the other still-unemitted variants' allows intact. Keep the exhaustive `no_core_event_variant_carries_secret_material` test's match arms compiling (ProvidersChanged already appears there).

DIAGNOSTICS - ERRORS NEAR THE CHAT PICKER: Verify features/model-selector/ProviderEnumerationErrors.tsx is rendered in the chat model-picker area (it is already used in PerMessageOverrideControl.tsx, which is rendered inside the Composer in the chat pane). With startup load() now running, a failing Ollama/cloud provider populates store.errors and these render as 'Couldn't load models from <providerId>: <reason>'. Confirm this path shows for the chat surface (not only Settings). If RoutingModeToggle is a more prominent surface, ALSO surface the errors there, but avoid duplicate stacked error lists in the same chat pane (PerMessageOverrideControl already owns one; keep a single visible instance, consistent with the existing NoModelsEmptyState de-duplication note in RoutingModeToggle).

DIAGNOSTICS - REFRESH AFFORDANCE: Add a lightweight, always-available 'Refresh models' control near the chat picker (e.g. a small button in PerMessageOverrideControl's header or adjacent to the picker) that calls the providers store load() (via useProvidersStore selector or getState().load()). This gives the user (our only live test rig) a way to re-enumerate on demand. Keep it unobtrusive and accessible (button with an aria-label). Optionally add a per-provider diagnostics line in Settings (ProviderKeysSection and/or LocalRuntimesSection) showing, per configured provider id, whether it enumerated and how many models, or the error - built ONLY from the display-safe store models/errors (never render resolved secrets). Keep additions minimal and token-styled to match existing components.

IPC / REGISTRATION: No new Tauri command is required (list_available_models / listAvailableModels and the mutation commands already exist). Do NOT add a command or touch generate_handler! unless you genuinely add one; if you do, register it in crates/tauri-app/src/lib.rs AND add a typed wrapper in frontend/src/ipc/commands.ts.

FRONTEND TESTS: Update app.test.tsx and any picker/settings test that mounts affected components so a NEW startup load() does not make `invoke` resolve undefined: ensure the `invoke` mock routes list_available_models to a well-formed { models, errors } for EVERY such test (app.test.tsx's routeInvoke already returns { models: [], errors: [] } - keep it). In app.test.tsx's 'SINGLE core-event subscription' test, the seeded spy `load` will now ALSO be called on startup; confirm the existing assertions still hold (it asserts listen called once and that a providersChanged event calls load) and ADD an explicit assertion that mounting <App/> calls the providers store load() at startup (e.g. seed a spy load via useProvidersStore.setState({ load }) and expect(load).toHaveBeenCalled() after render, using await waitFor/findBy for anything async). Add a test for the Refresh affordance: clicking it calls load() (spy) / triggers a list_available_models invoke. Add a test that store.errors render near the chat picker as the 'Couldn't load models from ...' line. Any assertion after a state change must use await findBy*/waitFor.

BACKEND TESTS: In crates/tauri-app/src/commands.rs tests, assert that the provider-config mutations emit CoreEvent::ProvidersChanged. AppState::new returns (Self, rx) where rx is the UnboundedReceiver<CoreEvent>; the existing test_state() helper drops rx (`let (state, _rx) = ...`). Add focused tests that KEEP the receiver, drive the mutation (via the _inner body plus the wrapper's emit, or via a small helper that performs the mutation then emits, matching however you wired step 3), and assert rx.try_recv()/recv() yields CoreEvent::ProvidersChanged. If you emit only in the #[tauri::command] wrapper (not _inner), add a helper or test that exercises the emit path directly so the behavior is covered without a live Tauri State. Ensure the orchestrator-core events.rs secret-hygiene test still compiles/passes after removing the allow.

SELF-AUDIT (the FOUR-CI-cycles guard): After edits, exhaustively review for (i) Rust clippy -D warnings: no unused imports (if CoreEvent/ProvidersChanged usage changes an import need, fix the `use`), no unused vars; (ii) eslint @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars: no unused TS imports/vars introduced (e.g. an unused useProvidersStore selector); (iii) tsc strict: types line up (load returns Promise<void>; store selectors typed); (iv) vitest mock completeness: trace EVERY test that mounts an affected component and confirm its `invoke` mock returns a well-formed shape for list_available_models and any refresh call. Run the offline checks recorded in FEAT-001 (per-crate `cargo fmt --check` for tauri-app + orchestrator-core; frontend `npx prettier --check .` if node_modules present) and fix any formatting.

SPEC: Update .kiro/specs/hybrid-orchestrator/architecture.md - in Section 7.3 (core state vs frontend state / event fan-out) and Section 8.2 (model selector) document that the providers store is loaded once at app startup (so the chat picker is populated without opening Settings) and that provider-config mutations emit CoreEvent::ProvidersChanged to trigger a refetch; note the always-available Refresh affordance and that enumeration errors surface near the chat picker. Add a phase/section to .kiro/specs/hybrid-orchestrator/tasks.md describing this fix, its acceptance (startup load, ProvidersChanged emit on the six/eight mutations, visible errors + refresh), and its CI gates. Do not use em dashes.
acceptance_criteria: On app startup, useProvidersStore.load() runs exactly once (verified by an app.test.tsx assertion), so the chat picker reads a populated models list without the user opening Settings.
app.tsx still opens exactly ONE onCoreEvent subscription (the existing 'SINGLE core-event subscription' test remains green) and it is torn down once on unmount.

crates/tauri-app/src/commands.rs emits CoreEvent::ProvidersChanged after successful set_cloud_provider, clear_cloud_provider, set_local_runtime, clear_local_runtime, import_embedded_model, select_embedded_model, load_embedded_model, and unload_embedded_model, verified by tauri-app unit test(s) that drain the core_events receiver.
CoreEvent::ProvidersChanged no longer carries #[allow(dead_code)] in orchestrator-core/src/events.rs, and the crate's secret-hygiene exhaustiveness test still compiles and passes.

Provider enumeration errors (store.errors) render near the CHAT model picker as 'Couldn't load models from <providerId>: <reason>' once load() has run and a provider fails, without a duplicate stacked error list in the same pane.
An always-available 'Refresh models' affordance near the chat picker calls the providers store load() (verified by a vitest test) so the user can re-enumerate on demand.
No plaintext secret or resolved SecretRef is ever rendered by any new/changed UI (diagnostics are built only from display-safe models/errors).
No new Tauri command is added (or, if one is, it is in generate_handler! AND has a typed IPC wrapper); serde boundary stays camelCase.
.kiro/specs/hybrid-orchestrator/architecture.md (Sections 7.3 and 8.2) and tasks.md document the startup load, the ProvidersChanged emit, the refresh affordance, and the visible errors.

Document the trace of each updated test mock.

findings.summary: Implemented both bug A (no startup load) and bug B (no ProvidersChanged emit), added a Refresh affordance, verified errors surface near the chat picker, updated tests + spec. Committed locally; not pushed.
findings.bug_a_startup_load: frontend/src/app.tsx: the SINGLE root useEffect (empty deps, the one onCoreEvent subscription) now also calls `void useProvidersStore.getState().load()` once at startup, before opening the subscription. The subscription semantics are unchanged (opened once, torn down once via the returned cleanup); the fan-out to every store's applyCoreEvent is untouched. Module header + inline comment document the startup hydration.
findings.bug_b_providers_changed_emit: crates/tauri-app/src/commands.rs: added a private `emit_providers_changed(state: &AppState)` helper that does `let _ = state.core_events.send(orchestrator_core::CoreEvent::ProvidersChanged);` (fire-and-forget, mirroring the existing McpStateChanged sends). It is called in the thin #[tauri::command] wrappers AFTER the _inner body returns Ok (so a validation/persist error emits nothing and the _inner unit tests are unchanged) for: set_cloud_provider, clear_cloud_provider, set_local_runtime, clear_local_runtime, import_embedded_model, select_embedded_model, load_embedded_model, unload_embedded_model. Each wrapper now binds the _inner result (`let view = _inner(...).await?;`), emits, then returns Ok(view).
findings.dead_code_allow_removed: crates/orchestrator-core/src/events.rs: removed the `#[allow(dead_code)]` and 'no emitter wired yet' comment on CoreEvent::ProvidersChanged (now emitted cross-crate from tauri-app, so it is not dead) and added a doc comment naming the emitters. Updated the module header from 'four still-unemitted variants' to 'three' (ConversationCreated/ConversationDeleted/PersonasChanged keep their allows). The exhaustive no_core_event_variant_carries_secret_material test still lists ProvidersChanged in both the events array and the match, so it keeps compiling.
findings.diagnostics_errors_near_picker: ProviderEnumerationErrors is already rendered inside PerMessageOverrideControl (in the Composer, chat pane). With startup load() now running in the chat context, store.errors populate and render as 'Couldn't load models from <providerId>: <message>'. No duplicate error list added elsewhere (RoutingModeToggle does not render errors and already dedupes the empty state). Did NOT add the optional Settings per-provider diagnostics line (kept scope minimal; existing Settings diagnostics already render errors via the same component).
findings.refresh_affordance: PerMessageOverrideControl gained a small always-available button with aria-label='Refresh models' (data-testid='refresh-models', class per-message-override__refresh) in the header that calls `void load()` (providers store selector). Minimal token-styled CSS added in styles/app.css (margin-left:auto to sit at the trailing edge; base button styling inherited from the existing .per-message-override__header button rules).
findings.no_new_command: No new Tauri command added (list_available_models/listAvailableModels and the mutation commands already exist), so generate_handler! and ipc/commands.ts were not touched. serde boundary unchanged (camelCase).
findings.frontend_tests: app.test.tsx: captured the real load() before tests (const realProvidersLoad) and restore it in beforeEach (useProvidersStore.setState({ models: [], load: realProvidersLoad })) so a seeded spy never leaks across tests. Added a new test asserting mounting <App/> calls the providers store load() once at startup (await waitFor). Updated the 'SINGLE core-event subscription' test: it now asserts load called exactly once at mount (startup) and TWICE after a providersChanged event (startup + event refetch), while keeping listen==1 and unlisten not called across nav. model-selector.test.tsx: captured/restored the real load() in resetStores; added a test that clicking 'Refresh models' re-runs list_available_models via the store and populates the picker, and a test that the Refresh control calls a spy load(). The existing tests already cover errors rendering near the picker (kept).
findings.backend_tests: commands.rs test module: added `test_state_with_rx()` (keeps the UnboundedReceiver<CoreEvent> that the shared test_state() drops) and an `assert_providers_changed(&mut rx)` helper; imported `CoreEvent` and `UnboundedReceiver` in the test module use-block. Added tests: set_cloud_provider / clear_cloud_provider / set_local_runtime / clear_local_runtime each emit ProvidersChanged (driving _inner then emit_providers_changed, mirroring the wrapper); embedded_model_mutations_emit_providers_changed covers import/select/load/unload; rejected_mutation_does_not_emit_providers_changed drives a non-cloud kind (Ollama) through set_cloud_provider_inner, asserts InvalidArgument, and asserts rx.try_recv().is_err() (nothing emitted on error).
findings.spec_updates: architecture.md Section 7.3 gained an 'Event fan-out and startup hydration' paragraph (single subscription + startup providers load() + ProvidersChanged emit list + Refresh affordance) and its event list now includes providers_changed; Section 8.2 gained a 'Populated on launch, refreshed on change (no dead picker)' bullet and the Events-consumed line notes providers_changed is now actually emitted. tasks.md gained 'Phase 11: Model picker startup population and refresh-on-change' (P11.1 startup load, P11.2 emit + allow removal, P11.3 visible errors + Refresh), with deliverable/parallelization/verification and a Future-work note recording that bundling Ollama and an HTML5 rewrite were considered and rejected (out of scope). No em dashes in any addition (the one pre-existing em dash at tasks.md P9.4 was not introduced by this task).
